title: Sprout and Cavolo Nero Pakora Nests
tagline: Winter greens, dressed up for a party. Crisp, gold, slightly smug.
servings: Serves 4 as a snack or starter

ingredients.item: Brussels sprouts, trimmed and finely shredded
cavolo nero, stalks removed, leaves finely shredded
fresh ginger, peeled and finely grated
ripe pears, cored and cut into small dice
cold water, plus 3 tbsp for the chutney

steps: Toast the cumin seeds in a dry saucepan for 30 seconds until fragrant. Tip half onto a plate. Leave the rest in the pan.
Chutney: add half the ginger, the pears, vinegar, 3 tbsp water and a pinch of the salt to the pan. Simmer 15 minutes, stirring, until soft and jammy.
Whisk the gram flour, remaining salt, reserved cumin and remaining ginger with 170 ml cold water into a thick, smooth batter. Rest it for 10 minutes.
Fold the shredded sprouts and cavolo nero into the batter until every strand is coated. Add a spoonful more water only if it feels stiff.
Heat the oil in a wide, heavy pan over a medium heat. Drop in loose, tangled spoonfuls. Fry 3 to 4 minutes per side, in batches, until deep gold and crisp.
Drain on kitchen paper, break one open to check the middle is cooked through, and serve hot with the warm pear chutney.
image_prompt: A rustic plate piled with tangled, deep golden pakora fritters studded with ribbons of dark green cavolo nero and shredded sprouts, a small bowl of glossy amber spiced pear chutney beside them, flecks of cumin seed visible, a few crisp frilly edges, steam rising.
alt_text: A plate of crisp golden vegetable fritters flecked with dark green cavolo nero, served with a bowl of amber pear chutney.
caption_hook:
Brussels sprouts at a Diwali-style feast. Hear me out: shredded, battered and fried, they're the first thing to vanish.
Who's the sprout sceptic at your table?
